To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cDNA for stromelysin was cloned from a human fibrosarcoma cell line, that the cDNA was sequenced and found to contain an open reading frame encoding an 11.5 kDa protein with a putative zinc-binding domain, that the stromelysin gene was found to be highly conserved in human and rat cells, that the stromelsin gene was expressed in a number of human cell lines and that stromelysin was shown to be a metalloproteinase with
the cDNA for human stromelysin encodes a protein that is 50% identical to human collagenase at the amino acid level.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the human stromelysin cDNA and the comparison of the amino acid sequences of stromelysin and of collagenase with the corresponding sequences of the N-terminal region of purified enzymes.
the identification of the genes that encode the human metalloproteinases, stromelysin and gelatinase.
the cloning and sequence analysis of human metalloproteinases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

stromelysin is a metalloproteinase which degrades extracellular matrix and basement membrane components, and that it is related to the family of metalloproteinases that includes the interstitial collagenases, the transin gene products and the matrix metalloproteinases (stromelysin and gelatinases).
the stromelysin and the collagenases represent a family of structurally and functionally related metalloproteinases.
the human stromelysin gene encodes a 52.5 kDa proenzyme, which is activated by limited proteolysis to a 45 kDa active enzyme, and that the human collagenase gene encodes a similar 45 kDa enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stromelysin and transin are identical proteins.

1) the human stromelysin gene is 15 kilobases long and contains eight exons; 2) the stromelysin mRNA is 1.7 kilobases long; 3) the stromelyin cDNA encodes a protein of 212 amino acids; 4) the stromelysins of human and rat are 80% identical at the amino acid level; 5) stromelysins are secreted as 45-kD proenz
the stromelysin gene is located on human chromosome 11 and that the human collagenase gene is located on chromosome 17.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have a better understanding of the role that these enzymes play in the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis.
we can use the same approach to identify the most effective treatment for patients who have been diagnosed with cancer.
the human stromelysin cDNA is highly homologous with the cDNA for the rat protein transin, and both are highly homologous to the cDNA for human XHF1.
